title: Pros, Cons, and Intuition — Aya Kim (Architecture candidate, 2nd loop)
body:
Purpose: quick, personal synth after the second loop with Aya (runtime architecture). This is intentionally raw — thoughts to share before we formalize a scorecard.

Context: Aya did a 90m deep-dive with me + Priya. Focus areas: latency SLOs at tail, KV-cache design for multi-tenant models, fallback routing and quantization strategies. Second loop targeted system design and operational tradeoffs; we also did a short whiteboard exercise on prefix caching behavior with partial responses.

High-level impression (gut):
- Strong systems instincts; thinks in constraints (PCIe bandwidth, PCIe <-> GPU mem migration, host vs device batching).
- Excellent at surfacing failure modes I hadn’t thought to prioritize (e.g., KV cache cold-shard pressure during canary rollouts).
- Communication: concise and pragmatic, but sometimes jumps to an implementation preference too quickly (prefers device-local embeddings for speed, didn’t fully explore hybrid-host options before committing).

Technical strengths observed:
- Latency and cost tradeoffs: clear mental model of tokens/sec vs batch size tradeoffs and when batching kills tail latency. Gave a concrete heuristic: limit continuous batching when 95th > 300ms, fallback to per-request pipeline for 50ms-sensitive routes.
- KV cache scaling: suggested sharding by request affinity (customer-session) rather than by KV-key range to reduce cross-shard hotness during popular prefixes. Good call for our multi-tenant traffic patterns.
- Quantization-aware routing: proposed runtime flags to prefer int8 variants for background tasks and fp16 for critical paths, with automatic warm-up thresholds based on observed perplexity drift.
- Observability focus: wanted richer per-token tracing (not just per-request), argued it’s critical for root-cause when partial responses are emitted.

Areas of concern / open questions:
- Implementation pragmatism: when pressured on timelines, Aya defaulted to custom in-house components rather than leveraging existing OSS libs (e.g., preferred writing a bespoke shard coordinator vs adapting existing placement libs). Risk: good long-term design but potential for scope creep on near-term deliveries.
- Security/compliance: less emphasis on auditability/KMS integration at architecture level; when asked explicitly, she sketched an approach but not a full threat model. For Private deployments we’ll need more detail.
- Team fit risk: her pattern is architect-heavy (prefers detailed design docs). Might be a mismatch for a delivery-heavy team that needs fast, pragmatic shipping.

Whiteboard exercise notes (prefix caching thought experiment):
- Problem given: design prefix/KV cache strategy to reduce per-token compute for chat sessions with mixed short and long contexts.
- Aya’s approach: multi-tier cache with LRU on device memory, a shared host-level cold-tier with probabilistic prefetch for predicted next-token keys. Prefetch heuristic based on transition probabilities from recent 3-token n-gram windows.
- Pros: reduces device cache misses when session exhibits locality; prefetch reduces cold-start latency for high affinity sessions.
- Cons flagged by Aya: prefetch may increase DRAM pressure and network egress; needs throttling policy per-tenant.
- My note: elegant idea; need experiments to measure prefetch hit rate vs added throughput cost. Worth an RTT proof-of-concept in staging.

Behavioral / leadership signals:
- Mentoring: gave a clear rubric for code review for junior engineers (tests + complexity budget + invariants), good sign for team-level coaching.
- Cross-team work: proactive about aligning with SRE and infra; asked pointed questions about our deployment ops and canary rollback windows.
- Decision making: prefers data-driven arguments; asked for telemetry baselines before committing to big-change rollouts.

Proposed score (informal):
- Technical: 4/5 (strong architecture, slight pragmatism gap)
- Execution: 3/5 (concern about delivering quickly with existing team cadence)
- Culture/communication: 4/5 (clear, works well with product + SRE)
- Overall recommendation: move to onsite/hire committee for role where there is time for architectural design and iterative shipping (e.g., runtime-architecture senior staff). If we need a fast-hitter senior IC for short deliverables, flag as caution.

Concrete follow-ups to resolve before final decision:
1) Ask Aya for a one-pager: "rollback-safe shard coordinator" that integrates with our autoscaler (JIRA INF-2147). Should include a threat model for private deployment (KMS, audit logs). Deadline: 2026-03-15.
2) Small take-home: design an experiment to measure prefetch hit rate for the n-gram heuristic on a sampled 7-day traffic trace. We should give access to sanitized samples and expect outline + expected metrics within 5 business days.
3) Pairing loop: 2-hour session with Priya to review a recent runtime incident (INC-762) and walk through operational runbooks to assess incident thinking.

Suggested interview panel changes if we progress:
- Add an SRE-focused interviewer to probe deployment and rollback mechanics.
- Add a security-focused interviewer for Private/KMS/audit concerns.

Notes to myself (things to remember in write-up):
- Emphasize Aya’s strength on KV cache heuristics — this maps to our Optimize roadmap and could reduce token cost by 3–7% for some workloads (convince finance).
- Call out the implementation risk — check manager’s appetite for multi-quarter infrastructure projects.
- Don’t over-index on the early preference for in-house components; probe more in the take-home.

Bottom line (one-liner to share with hiring committee): Aya is a high-quality architect with excellent runtime tradeoff instincts and clear mentoring skills; recommend moving forward if we can define a scoped, measurable evaluation (proof-of-concept + incident pairing) to validate pragmatic delivery and security thinking.

Draft comments I plan to paste into the panel doc: (short):
- "Aya shows deep latency/caching mental models and strong dev leadership. Recommend take-home + SRE/security pairing before final offer. Prioritize verification of KMS/audit integration and a small POC for prefetch heuristic."

Random scratch snippets (notes-to-self):
- Investigate: suspected impact of prefetch on checksum verification CPU spike (INC-447 analog).
- Link to traffic sample: gs://redwood-scratch/interview-samples/aya-7day-sample (ask infra to provision read-only)
- Possible scoring tweak: weight "execution" higher if role is IC3 (fast delivery) vs IC4 (architecture-heavy).

End of raw notes. Will tidy and submit to hiring doc tomorrow after Priya's comments.
